ai.title: GLM 5.1 session quota window shortened to 12 hours
ai.summary: The `z-ai/glm-5.1` rate limit window in `web/src/server/free-session/public-api.ts` drops from 20 to 12 hours, keeping the cap at 5 sessions. `fetchRateLimitSnapshot` now returns `windowMs` directly to prevent duplicated math in the `retryAfterMs` calculation. CLI comments in `waiting-room-screen.tsx` and `use-freebuff-session.ts` updated to reflect the new window. Docs and schema comments in `packages/internal/src/db/schema.ts` and `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` aligned.

eli5.text: If you're using the GLM 5.1 model, you'll now hit your usage limit sooner. You can still start 5 sessions (meetings with the AI), but they roll off a 12-hour window instead of the previous 20-hour window. So if you've been maxing out your 5 sessions, you'll need to wait a shorter time before slots free up and you can start a new one. The CLI now shows clearer messages about when your oldest session will expire and let you start again.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.51 release
ai.summary: Version 0.0.51 rolls up several user-facing Freebuff improvements shipped since 0.0.50. The CLI waiting-room screen now renders distinct messages for unverified countries and IP privacy signals (VPN, Tor, proxy, hosting) instead of generic unknown-location errors, backed by new `FreebuffCountryBlockReason` and `FreebuffIpPrivacySignal` enums in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` and parsing in `parseApiErrorResponseBody`. Free mode now fail-closed on unresolved countries and IPinfo VPN/proxy checks, requiring a new `IPINFO_TOKEN` env var. Kimi K2.6 routes through CanopyWave with updated per-million-token pricing ($0.95/$0.16/$4.00), and `z-ai/glm-5.1` sees its free-session rate limit window shortened from 20 to 12 hours with `fetchRateLimitSnapshot` returning `windowMs` directly. A new `waiting_room` ad surface was added to Gravity with forced choice variants and dedicated placement IDs.
ai.evidence: The diff shows a single line change in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumping the version field from `0.0.50` to `0.0.51`, with the commit analyzed as a release-bump within the Freebuff CLI release package.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.51 strengthens and expands the platform with important updates to how AI models are routed, how free access is controlled, and how users are guided through usage limits. Kimi K2.6 now runs through CanopyWave, which means you get faster and more reliable access to that model with updated pricing. Free mode now blocks traffic from VPNs, proxies, and unknown locations, making the service safer and fairer for everyone. The GLM 5.1 model's session quota window has been shortened to 12 hours, helping balance demand and availability. When you hit the waiting room because the system is busy, you now see a clearer message if your location can't be verified and a new ad surface appears during your wait. Upgrading gives you stronger security, smoother model access, and a more transparent experience when usage limits apply.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI shows specific VPN/Tor block reasons
ai.summary: Waiting-room screen now displays precise IP privacy signals (VPN, Tor, proxy) instead of generic unknown-location errors. `getCountryCodeFromFreeModeError` replaced by `getCountryBlockFromFreeModeError` in `error-handling.ts` to extract `countryBlockReason` and `ipPrivacySignals` from API responses. `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` defines new `FreebuffCountryBlockReason` and `FreebuffIpPrivacySignal` enums; `parseApiErrorResponseBody` in `common/src/util/error.ts` parses these fields. Scope: CLI waiting-room UI, error handling utils, common type definitions, session state.

eli5.text: When a user tries to use the service but is blocked by a waiting room screen due to their IP address being detected as coming through a VPN, Tor network, or proxy, the screen will now show the specific reason instead of a generic "unknown location" error message. The system now extracts precise information about which privacy tool or network is causing the block (like "VPN" or "Tor") and displays that directly to the user. If you were previously seeing a vague "location unknown" message when blocked, you'll now see exactly which privacy service is being flagged, helping you understand why access was denied and what you might need to change.

ai.title: Disable GLM dedicated Fireworks deployment
ai.summary: GLM 5.1 (`z-ai/glm-5.1`) now routes through Fireworks serverless API during availability hours, bypassing the dedicated deployment `mjb4i7ea`. This change is driven by a new `FIREWORKS_HOURS_GATED_MODELS` set in `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts` that enforces hour-gating for `FREEBUFF_GLM_MODEL_ID` even on serverless, overriding the previous deployment-hour check. The update affects `web/src/llm-api/fireworks-config.ts` (commented out deployment map) and `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts` (fallback logic). Deployment-mapped models still never fall back to serverless API during cooldown or after 5xx errors.

eli5.text: The GLM 5.1 assistant now serves requests through the standard public access hours instead of a private reserved connection that was active all the time. If you use GLM 5.1, your requests will only be processed during Freebuff's published availability hours, even though they are now handled by the shared public system rather than the dedicated one. The private connection itself is turned off and no longer accepts traffic.

eli5.text: This release makes it clearer when your connection is being blocked for privacy reasons, so you are less likely to be left guessing why access was denied. FreeBuff now explains exactly why you might be blocked - for example, if you are using a VPN, Tor network, or proxy - instead of showing a vague error message. Behind the scenes, the AI model called GLM has switched to running through a serverless cloud service, which can improve reliability during certain hours. These changes mean you get more helpful error messages when your network setup triggers a block, and the system keeps working more smoothly when AI model demand shifts throughout the day.

ai.title: Harden Freebuff country gating
ai.summary: Added strict country and IP privacy checks to `POST /session`, failing closed on unresolved IPs or lookup errors. Introduced `ip_privacy_lookup_failed` block reason and expanded `free_session` table with columns for `country_code`, `cf_country`, `geoip_country`, `country_block_reason`, `ip_privacy_signals`, `client_ip_hash`, and `country_checked_at` via migration `0047_tough_silver_fox.sql`. Covers `packages/internal`, `web`, and `common` types; updates `docs/freebuff-waiting-room.md`.

eli5.text: If you try to start a free session, the system now does a stricter check on your country and IP address before letting you in. If it can’t figure out where you’re connecting from or if privacy-protection tools like VPNs or Tor are detected, it blocks you by default instead of guessing. The system remembers the result of this check (without storing your actual IP address) so it can be reviewed later, and it records a specific reason for any block. This affects anyone trying to start a free session through the waiting room.
